cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This cafe chair wobbles. I've approved taking all the chairs apart to check their joints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we leave the others? I tested them. It's this one floorboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chairs may remain intact. I authorize lifting the floor; your test has identified the real opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're supposed to open in twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Closure is approved. You may put up the sign while I mark a new position for the counter. A bare floor lets us solve the queue as well.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 grants sparing the chairs by authorizing floor removal; A5 approves closure and uses the exposed floor to expand into counter layout.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 isolated-board test causes A3 wider floor work; B4 imminent opening causes A5 closure and still broader renovation.

relationship.evidence: B2 has tested the furniture and B4 protects operating hours, plausibly trying to contain scope.

heightening.evidence: B4 deadline becomes A5 a closure decision that permits a larger project instead of limiting it.

specificity.evidence: A1 cafe chair, B2 one board and B4 twenty-minute opening establish the practical scale and cost.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 solve-the-queue-as-well is earned by the proposed floor access and counter move, not a separate arbitrary mishap.
